Routine Descriptions

SRSCAN_ASI_KEOGRAM

 [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_asi_keogram

PURPOSE:
  Build a custom keogram from a loaded raw all-sky image variable: a
  vertical (south-north) slice through each frame, stacked in time.

  Unlike the archived keogram products (lossy JPEG quicklooks for TREx
  RGB), a keogram built here from raw data is photometric -- this is the
  quantitative alternative the loaders point at.

  Works on truecolor cubes {x[n], y[n,3,ncol,nrow]} (TREx RGB); creates
    <varname>_keo: {x[n], y[n,nrow,3] byte, v[nrow]}
  which renders in TRUECOLOR in tplot (srscan_trexrgb_keoplot plotting
  routine; the zrange option sets the linear stretch). With channel= set,
  a single-channel classic spectrogram companion <varname>_keo_<channel>
  is created as well. Row 0 = south, matching the archived keogram
  convention, so the two can be compared directly.

INPUT:
  varname: raw image tplot variable, e.g. 'srscan_trexrgb_gill'

KEYWORDS:
  column:  CCD column to slice (default: center column)
  channel: if set to 'luma', 'r', 'g', or 'b', also create the
           single-channel spectrogram companion
  newname: output variable base name (default <varname>_keo)
  verbose: dprint verbosity

EXAMPLE:
  srscan_load_trex_rgb, site='gill', trange=['2023-03-24/06:00','2023-03-24/07:00']
  srscan_asi_keogram, 'srscan_trexrgb_gill'
  tplot, 'srscan_trexrgb_gill_keo'

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_asi_keogram.pro)

SRSCAN_LOAD_TREX_RGB

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_load_trex_rgb

PURPOSE:
  Load TREx RGB all-sky imager data from the data archive at
  data.phys.ucalgary.ca (file listings via api.phys.ucalgary.ca).

  Datatypes:
    'raw'     (default) stream0 truecolor images, nominal 3-s cadence
              -> srscan_trexrgb_<site>  {x[n], y[n,3,553,480] byte}
              MEMORY: ~0.95 GB per site-hour; load minutes, or time=
    'keogram' archived hourly keogram JPEGs (quicklook DN, lossy)
              -> srscan_trexrgb_keo_<site>  {x[n], y[n,480,3] byte}
              renders TRUECOLOR in tplot (srscan_trexrgb_keoplot routine;
              the zrange option sets the linear stretch); channel= adds a
              single-channel spectrogram companion
    'grid'    pre-rendered MOSv001 global mosaic grids (selected
              intervals only)
              -> srscan_trexrgb_grid  {x[n], y[n,3,1024,512] float}

KEYWORDS:
  site:         4-letter site code(s): string, array, space-delimited
                list, or 'all' (default). Ignored for datatype='grid'.
  datatype:     'raw' (default), 'keogram', 'grid', or 'all'-style lists
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); only the file
                granules covering the range are fetched, and the output
                is clipped to trange unless /no_time_clip is set
  no_time_clip: store everything in the fetched files instead of
                clipping the output to trange (output then aligns to
                file boundaries: 1-min for raw/grid, hourly for keogram)
  time:         single time: load only the frame nearest this time
                (+-1.5 s; raw only)
  channel:      keogram only: if set to 'luma', 'r', 'g', or 'b', also
                create a single-channel classic spectrogram companion
                srscan_trexrgb_keo_<site>_<channel> (the main keogram
                variable is always full RGB)
  suffix:       appended to tplot variable names
  downloadonly: download but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  offline mode; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files:        (out) local paths of the files used (assigned once per call)
  relpathnames_all: (out) cache-relative paths (assigned once per call);
                requesting this implies downloadonly + no_download
  tplotnames:   (out) names of the tplot variables created
  valid_names:  print/return the valid sites and datatypes without loading
                (site and datatype keywords are assigned the valid lists)

EXAMPLES:
  timespan, '2023-03-24', 1, /day
  srscan_load_trex_rgb, datatype='keogram'                    ; all sites
  srscan_load_trex_rgb, site='gill', $
    trange=['2023-03-24/06:20', '2023-03-24/06:30']           ; 10 min raw
  srscan_load_trex_rgb, time='2023-03-24/06:22:30'            ; one frame,
                                                              ; all sites

NOTES:
  Burst data (stream0.burst) and the early legacy-PGM era are not
  supported. Data documentation: https://data.phys.ucalgary.ca

SRSCAN_TREXRGB_KEOPLOT

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trexrgb_keoplot

PURPOSE:
  Custom tplot plotting routine that renders a TRUECOLOR (RGB) keogram
  panel. Registered on a tplot variable through
    dlimits = {tplot_routine: 'srscan_trexrgb_keoplot', ...}
  and invoked by tplot itself; not normally called by users.

  Expects data {x[n], y[n,nrow,3], v[nrow]} -- time, pixel row
  (south->north), RGB channel. The panel is painted with tv,/true in
  24-bit color, so keograms look like the archive colour quicklooks
  instead of a greyscale spectrogram.

  Honored limits/dlimits options (beyond the standard axis options that
  box/plot understand: yrange, ytitle, position, ...):
    zrange:  [lo,hi] linear DN stretch window applied to all three
             channels (default [0,255]; one window preserves colour
             balance)
    datagap: seconds; gaps longer than this render black
             (default 2x the median sample spacing)

  Requires a 24-bit graphics target. WIN/X are fine as-is; for headless
  Z-buffer rendering use
    device, set_resolution=[xs,ys], set_pixel_depth=24, decomposed=0
  (tv,/true paints real RGB on any 24-bit target regardless of the
  decomposed setting, and decomposed=0 keeps tplot's axis/label colors
  going through the color table as usual -- with decomposed=1 the axis
  color index 255 would be read as the 24-bit value '0000FF'x = red).
  If truecolor display fails (8-bit device), the routine falls back to a
  greyscale luma rendering through the current color table and says so.

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trexrgb_keoplot.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_LOAD_GRID

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_load_grid

PURPOSE:
  Load TREx RGB pre-rendered mosaic grids (MOSv001) from the data
  archive (data.phys.ucalgary.ca) into a tplot variable:
    srscan_trexrgb_grid: {x[n], y[n,3,1024,512] float, v1[3], v2[1024], v3[512]}

  The grids are the OFFICIAL archive mosaic product: all available
  cameras projected at 110 km onto a global geographic grid of
  1024 x 512 (lon x lat) cells, 0.3515625 deg/cell, fill value -999 where
  no camera maps. One 1-min HDF5 file holds 20 frames (3-s cadence).
  The archive stores the lat axis north-first; the loader applies the
  standard orient transform so index j increases NORTHWARD in the tplot
  variable (lat = -90 + (j+0.5)*cell), consistent with everything else.
  Grids are produced only for SELECTED intervals (e.g. 2023-03-23/24);
  an empty result for other dates is expected, and the loader says so.

  MEMORY NOTE: one minute is ~120 MB as float; load short windows or use
  time= for a single frame.

  Grid geometry (lon/lat cell edges, fill value) is carried in dlimits.

  Internal worker for srscan_load_trex_rgb.

KEYWORDS:
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); whole 1-min files
                covering the range are fetched and the output is clipped
                to trange unless /no_time_clip is set
  no_time_clip: store every frame of every fetched file instead of
                clipping the output to trange (output then aligns to
                1-min file boundaries)
  time:         load only the single frame nearest this time (+-1.5 s);
                output y is [3,1024,512]
  suffix:       appended to the tplot variable name
  downloadonly: download files but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  do not contact server; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files, relpathnames_all: (in/out) append contract (see load_raw header)
  tplotnames:   (out) accumulates created tplot variable names

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_load_grid.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_LOAD_KEOGRAM

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_load_keogram

PURPOSE:
  Load TREx RGB archived hourly keograms from the data archive
  (data.phys.ucalgary.ca), stitched across the requested range, into:
    srscan_trexrgb_keo_<site>: {x[n], y[n,480,3] byte, v[480]}
  The variable renders in TRUECOLOR in tplot (like the archive colour
  quicklooks) through the srscan_trexrgb_keoplot plotting routine
  registered in its dlimits; the zrange option sets the linear stretch.
  With channel= set, a single-channel classic spectrogram companion
  srscan_trexrgb_keo_<site>_<channel> {x[n], y[n,480] byte} (spec=1) is
  created as well.

  IMPORTANT -- these keograms are lossy JPEG QUICKLOOK products: the DN
  values carry JPEG compression artifacts and display scaling, and are
  NOT photometric. Structure and timing are correct -- they plot
  correctly and are ideal for browsing -- but do not use the values as
  intensities. For quantitative work build a keogram from the raw images
  (srscan_asi_keogram on a loaded srscan_trexrgb_<site> variable).

  Layout facts (pinned empirically against the archive):
    - hourly files, 1200 columns/hour = one column per 3-s frame;
      column j is the frame at hour_start + j*3 s (zero offset)
    - as read by read_jpeg, row 0 = south, so the tplot spectrogram
      (row index increasing upward) is already north-at-top; no flip

  Internal worker for srscan_load_trex_rgb.

KEYWORDS:
  sites:        string array of 4-letter site codes (lowercase)
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); output is clipped
                to trange unless /no_time_clip is set (keograms are
                cheap; matches thm_load_ask)
  no_time_clip: store every column of every fetched hourly file instead
                of clipping the output to trange
  channel:      if set to 'luma', 'r', 'g', or 'b', ALSO create a
                single-channel spectrogram companion variable
                srscan_trexrgb_keo_<site>_<channel> (the main variable
                is always full RGB)
  suffix:       appended to tplot variable names
  downloadonly: download files but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  do not contact server; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files:        (in/out) APPENDS local file paths (assign-once handled by
                the public loader; see srscan_trex_rgb_load_raw header)
  relpathnames_all: (in/out) same contract
  tplotnames:   (out) accumulates created tplot variable names

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_load_keogram.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_LOAD_RAW

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_load_raw

PURPOSE:
  Load TREx RGB raw (stream0 nominal cadence) truecolor images from the
  data archive (data.phys.ucalgary.ca) into tplot variables:
    srscan_trexrgb_<site>: {x: double[n], y: byte[n,3,553,480],
                            v1: [3], v2: [553], v3: [480]}
  Frames are ORIENTed (north-up/east-right): reform(y[i,*,*,*]) is a
  [3,553,480] truecolor frame ready for tv,/true.

  This is an internal worker for srscan_load_trex_rgb; users should call
  srscan_load_trex_rgb.

  MEMORY NOTE: one hour of one site is ~1200 frames x 0.8 MB = ~0.95 GB.
  Load short windows (minutes) or use time= for single frames.

KEYWORDS:
  sites:        string array of 4-letter site codes (lowercase)
  trange:       time range (defaults to timerange()); whole 1-min files
                covering the range are fetched and the output is clipped
                to trange unless /no_time_clip is set
  no_time_clip: store every frame of every fetched file instead of
                clipping the output to trange (output then aligns to
                1-min file boundaries)
  time:         load only the single frame nearest this time (+-1.5 s);
                output y is [3,553,480], the single-record convention
  suffix:       appended to tplot variable names
  downloadonly: download files but do not load into tplot
  no_download:  do not contact server; use only the local cache
  verbose:      dprint verbosity
  files:        (in/out) APPENDS local file paths across sites. The public
                loader collects these in a local and assigns its own files
                keyword once per call (the GUI reuses one variable per
                load, so appending at the public level would grow it)
  relpathnames_all: (in/out) accumulates cache-relative paths, same contract
  tplotnames:   (out) accumulates created tplot variable names

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_load_raw.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_ORIENT

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_trex_rgb_orient

PURPOSE:
  The one authoritative orientation transform for TREx RGB image and
  skymap arrays. Apply it to EVERYTHING with a pixel-y dimension (raw
  frames, skymap lat/lon/elevation grids, corner grids) and the arrays
  line up with each other and render north-up/east-right with tv,/true
  (matching the archive quicklook orientation).

  As stored in the archive files, x increases eastward and y increases
  SOUTHWARD; the fix is a flip of the y dimension:
    [553,480]  or [554,481]   2-D grids   -> reverse(a, 2)
    [3,553,480]               one frame   -> reverse(a, 3)
    [n,3,553,480]             frame cube  -> reverse(a, 4)
  i.e. always the LAST dimension, which is what this function does.

  NOTE: this is a pure y-flip (reverse), NOT the 180-degree rotation
  (rotate(img,2)) that THEMIS ASI and REGO need -- the TREx RGB x axis is
  already east-positive. Pinned empirically against the archived hourly
  keograms and mosaic grids.

INPUT:
  img: 2-D, 3-D, or 4-D array in archive orientation (any numeric type)

OUTPUT:
  The array with the y (last) dimension reversed.

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_orient.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_READFILE

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
PROCEDURE:
  srscan_trex_rgb_readfile

PURPOSE:
  Read TREx RGB stream0 (nominal cadence) HDF5 files into a frame cube
  and a matching unix-time array.

  Each 1-minute file holds up to 20 truecolor frames (nominal 3-s
  cadence) in /data/images as byte [nf,3,553,480] -- frame index first,
  then [channel, x, y] -- plus /data/timestamp, an array of strings of
  the form 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff UTC' giving each frame's exposure
  start. Short files (fewer than 20 frames) occur and are handled.

  Frames are returned in ARCHIVE orientation (y increases southward);
  apply srscan_trex_rgb_orient before display or geometry work.

INPUT:
  filenames: string array of local .h5 file paths

OUTPUT (positional):
  images:   byte array [n_frames, 3, 553, 480]
  times:    dblarr [n_frames], unix time of each frame

KEYWORDS:
  count:    (out) number of frames read
  verbose:  dprint verbosity passthrough

NOTES:
  File layout verified against the archive with h5_parse (2023-03-24
  gill). Files that fail to open or lack the expected datasets are
  skipped with a warning rather than aborting the read.

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_readfile.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_SITES

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_trex_rgb_sites

PURPOSE:
  Return the table of TREx RGB all-sky imager sites. This is the ONE
  authoritative site list for the srs_canada TREx RGB routines: the
  loaders, mosaic driver, and map defaults all resolve sites against this
  function, so site changes are one-line edits here.

OUTPUT:
  Array of structures {uid, name, glat, glon} with geographic latitude
  (deg) and east longitude (deg, -180..180).

NOTES:
  Coordinates are the nominal site locations; the per-site skymap files
  (srscan_trex_rgb_skymap) carry the precise calibrated values and are
  what the mosaic geometry actually uses.

EXAMPLE:
  sites = srscan_trex_rgb_sites()
  print, sites.uid

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_sites.pro)

SRSCAN_TREX_RGB_SKYMAP

 [Previous Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_trex_rgb_skymap

PURPOSE:
  Locate, download, and restore the best TREx RGB skymap for a site at a
  given time (latest validity start at or before the time; see
  srscan_skymap for the selection rule).

  The returned structure is the native skymap: fields include
  full_map_latitude/full_map_longitude ([554,481,n_alt] corner grids at
  the project altitudes), full_elevation/full_azimuth ([553,480]),
  site_map_latitude/site_map_longitude, generation info, etc.

  NOTE: the arrays are in ARCHIVE orientation; apply
  srscan_trex_rgb_orient to any array with a pixel-y dimension before
  combining with ORIENTed images.

INPUT:
  site: 4-letter site code, e.g. 'gill' (string)
  time: requested time (double unix time or string)

KEYWORDS:
  no_download: use only the local cache
  verbose:     dprint verbosity
  filename:    (out) local path of the restored skymap file

OUTPUT:
  the restored skymap structure, or -1 if none could be obtained

EXAMPLE:
  sky = srscan_trex_rgb_skymap('gill', '2023-03-24')
  help, sky, /structure

(See projects/srs_canada/asi/srscan_trex_rgb_skymap.pro)
